newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Riksbank seen having secret crown target.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Riksbank seen having secret crown target.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, has a secret target for the crown despite public statements that it has no set levels for the currency, analysts said.
The analysts, talking after the Riksbank was seen intervening to buy crown on Tuesday, said the target was around 4.30 versus the mark.

"On the contrary to what the Riksbank says, there is of course a target for the crown. It's hardly credible for them to talk about a stable currency while at the same time allowing the crown to fluctuate in a range of, say, 4.30 to 4.70 versus the mark," one analyst said.
Analysts said there might be a narrow range in which the central bank intervenes rather than a sinlge figure.
The Riksbank said last month it planned to be more active in currency markets to reduce volatility and increase crown stability.
Some other analysts argued, however, that the bank only had loose targets for the currency.
Sven Arne Svensson, economist at brokerage Hagstromer & Qviberg, said there appeared to be a floor rather than a target. "Don't let it go through 4.50 versus the mark," he said.

Bjorn Englund, economist at Unibank Markets, told Reuters: "I don't think the iomportance of intervention should be exaggerated. When the Riksbanken enter the market it intervenes for a very specific reason," he said.
Since saying it would intervene more regularly, the bank has been seen selling crown at 4.29 versus the mark to prevent the currency strengthening.

A few days later it was seen supporting the crown at a level around 4.32, a level which market players believed at first was a floor, but the currency soon weakened and Tuesday's intervention was seen at a 4.35 to the mark level.
The central bank refuses to comment on intervention.
